summary: The second session did what the empty-frontier rule asks. It loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development first, then made a new worktree and registered on the plan. `sdd-state next` returned `status=none reason=held`, so it posted a waiting record with `--kind tasks`, printed the board and handed back saying both tasks are held by fixture-session. It took no task over.
reasoning: Every criterion is backed by the session log or by files on disk. I never had to answer a takeover question or a confirmation prompt: the agent only listed takeover as an option and said it would act only on explicit approval.

observations.description: The worktree guard hook blocked `git switch --detach feature/parallel` twice. The agent said the guard seemed to read 'parallel' in the branch name as the GNU parallel tool. The agent got around it by detaching at the commit sha (bbf27e3). That is a false positive in the guard, and it would hit any plan or branch with 'parallel' in its name.

The agent's first combined Bash command (register plus a progress.md append via heredoc) was refused by the guard: 'runs a command whose name is computed at runtime inside a construct too complex to verify'. The agent split it into literal commands. This cost extra steps, but nothing went wrong.

Claude Code onboarding: on the trust and Bypass Permissions dialogs, 'No, exit' is selected by default. On my first launch, after I picked 'No' on the 'Newer Opus model available' prompt, Claude exited to the bash prompt but the old dialog was still drawn on screen. That made it look like Claude was still running, and I had to relaunch.
The 'Newer Opus model available' dialog said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. After the relaunch, the header showed Opus 5.5.
The hand-back message was clear. It gave the worktree path, what `next` returned and the board, and offered two options (wait, or take over only on explicit approval naming a task).
